newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson buy to dilute Lagardere results.
newsitem.headline: Thomson buy to dilute Lagardere results.

text.p: Lagardere's takeover of electronics firm Thomson SA will result in a "very slight dilution" of the missiles-to-media group's results for the next two years, Lagardere managing director Philippe Camus said on Wednesday.
"At the start, for the first two years, there will be a very slight dilution. Profits will rise but a little more slowly," he told a seminar organised by Paris brokerage Bourse Ferri.

He said the dilution would be between five and 10 percent. He said without the takeover of Thomson, Lagardere's profit would have been much larger thanks to gains from several big contracts, which he did not name.
"From 1999, we will harvest the effects of this merger operation. And then the results will be very significant," he said.

The French government plans to inject 11 billion french francs ($2.1 billion) in into Thomson before selling the electronics group to Lagardere for one franc. Lagardere plans to merge its Matra missiles unit with Thomson's Thomson-CSF defence electronics subsidiary after buying out minority shareholders and sell the Thomson Multimedia unit to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
